props.gloss_en: Beit Shammai (as R' Yehuda reports): [for a ceiling with no plaster] one loosens [the boards] and removes one from between them
Beit Hillel (as R' Yehuda reports): one loosens [them] OR removes one from between them
R' Meir: one removes one from between them, and does not [merely] loosen
one may roof [the sukkah] with boards -- R' Yehuda
and R' Meir forbids
Rav: the dispute concerns boards that have [a width of] four
Rav: [the 14a.10 dispute is because] R' Meir holds the decree of the roof and R' Yehuda does not
Shmuel: the dispute concerns boards that do not have four
Shmuel: but if they have four, all agree it is invalid
the stam: Beit Hillel's reason is 'you shall make' -- and not from what is already made; loosening is an act, removing one is an act
the stam: Beit Shammai's reason is, in fact, the decree of the roof
the stam's reading of Beit Shammai: even though one loosens, if he removes one from between them -- yes; if not -- no (removing one is what counts)
the stam's reading of R' Meir's clause: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not dispute in this matter
(what the seifa would teach) R' Meir holds the decree of the roof
(what the seifa would teach) and R' Yehuda does not hold the decree of the roof
R' Yochanan: the first clause (the 14a.10 mishnah) deals with planed boards
R' Yochanan: and it is on account of the decree of vessels that they touched on it
Rav: if one roofed it with male arrows, it is valid
Rav: with female arrows, it is invalid
the stam: and he did not decree against male [arrows] on account of female ones
the stam, according to Rav: here too, let us not decree against planed boards on account of vessels
the stam, according to Rav: and in the latter clause (15a.1) too they dispute the decree of the roof
the stam: the latter clause is R' Yehuda saying to R' Meir 'why do you forbid boards -- the roof decree? that is Beit Shammai's', and R' Meir answering 'they did not dispute in this matter'
(R' Yehuda, per the stam's reading) that reasoning is Beit Shammai's -- they hold the roof decree
(R' Yehuda, per the stam's reading) and Beit Hillel do not decree
the stam, according to Shmuel: they dispute the negation of [an existing] ceiling
one master holds: [the ceiling] is negated by this [loosening]
and the other master holds: by this it is not negated

objections.gloss_en: אלא בית שמאי מאי טעמייהו? אי משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי — בחדא סגי! אי משום גזרת תקרה — בנוטל אחת מבינתים סגי! -- neither available reason requires both acts

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם משום גזרת תקרה, והכי קאמרי: אף על פי שמפקפק, אי נוטל אחת מבינתים — אין, אי לא — לא (= p_bs_taam_tikra, p_bs_hachi_kamrei)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, אימא סיפא: רבי מאיר אומר נוטל אחת מבינתים אבל לא יפקפק — רבי מאיר היינו בית שמאי! (kind svara: the bite is drawn from the mishnah's own seifa, אימא סיפא, which has no ObjectionKind of its own)

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: לא נחלקו בית שמאי ובית הלל בדבר זה (= p_rm_hachi_kamar)

objections.gloss_en: הניחא לרב ... אלא שמואל, דאמר בשאין בהן ארבעה מחלוקת, אבל יש בהן ארבעה — דברי הכל פסולה, סיפא במאי פליגי? -- if both tannaim forbid four-wide boards, the seifa cannot be a dispute over the roof decree
